FPMC (2010) combines persistent user–item affinity with recent item-transition scores. FOSSIL (2016) is closer to an embedding-history baseline: a history-length-normalized sum of consumed-item embeddings plus a personalized weighted sum of recent embeddings. Neither explicitly evaluates normalized recent-minus-persistent histories; FOSSIL’s normalization controls history magnitude, rather than centering recent behavior. [FPMC](https://archives.iw3c2.org/www2010/pub/pdfs/RendleFreudenthaler2010-FPMC.pdf), [FOSSIL](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/icdm16a.pdf).

Gated comparators include SLi-Rec (2019), which adaptively fuses attentive long-term preferences and recurrent short-term preferences, and HGN (2019), which selects historical features/items through hierarchical gates. CLSR (2022) is especially relevant: it uses full-history and recent-history embedding averages as supervision proxies for separate interest encoders, then adaptively aggregates their outputs. These investigate separation and fusion, rather than an explicitly normalized difference vector. [SLi-Rec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2019/0585.pdf), [HGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217), [CLSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13090).

The closest verified subtraction-based comparator is BSARec (AAAI 2024): it separates low-frequency signals from complementary high-frequency residuals and learns their relative contribution alongside self-attention. FMLPRec (WWW 2022) also explicitly evaluates classical high-pass filtering, although its findings favor low-pass/band-stop filtering. Neither establishes the exact formulation normalize(recent average − persistent average), nor a centered causal EMA. Thus temporal high-pass recommendation already has precedent; the narrower normalized, causal history-centering formulation remains unverified by this search, not established as novel. Prioritize BSARec and CLSR alongside FOSSIL, and ablate uncentered EMA, centered EMA, normalization, and gated fusion under identical validation. [BSARec](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.10325v2), [FMLPRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13556).
